item.text: {"0":"Across all four datasets, remove the 0.5 ranking margin: use softplus(negative-positive)+0.2*[softplus(-positive)+softplus(negative)], averaged over existing nonpadding targets. This restores the previously successful objective while isolating its effect with the current untied normalized embeddings. Preserve architecture, scoring, optimizer, sampling and training settings.","1":"Across all four datasets, jointly set learning rate to 0.001 and dropout to 0.10, retaining batch size 128 and all other settings. Larger updates may accelerate adaptation of the independently parameterized input/output embeddings, while reduced dropout preserves their unit-normalized recurrent signal. Keep embedding design, loss, GRU topology, readout, seeds and training caps fixed.","2":"Across all four datasets, scale history embeddings by a deterministic training-frequency feature: clamp((median_positive_item_count/max(item_count,1))^0.10,0.8,1.2), with padding remaining zero. This tests gentler frequency correction than the previously regressing exponent 0.25. Derive counts solely from training interactions and checkpoint the scales for identical inference. Preserve learned embedding design, GRU topology, readout, candidate embeddings, loss and optimizer.","3":"Across all four datasets, replace dot-product compatibility with jointly trained residual bilinear compatibility: score(h,e)=(h+hW)·e, initializing W to zero. Apply the same transformation to every training position and the existing final-real-position inference state. This starts at incumbent scores while allowing recurrent states to align with the untied output embedding space. Preserve GRU recurrence, features, embeddings, readout selection, loss and optimizer; update checkpoint loading and predictor writing consistently."}
